claim_text_patches.text: Records the literal source item stem asking whether 'you' were approached by community and/or political party representatives; the addressee and report role (respondent vs interviewer, or other) are unresolved from the supplied metadata, which provides only the stem and 0/1 No/Yes labels.

Records the literal source item stem asking whether 'you' felt threatened during the interview; addressee and report role are unresolved from the supplied metadata, and the stem concerns felt threat rather than an observed physical act.

Records the literal source item stem asking whether 'you' were physically threatened during the interview; addressee and report role are unresolved from the supplied metadata, and the item is distinct from felt threat, with no nesting or co-occurrence relation inferred.

All three items share a 0/1 No/Yes response act, but the literal stems use 'you' with different referents (third-party approach, felt threat, physical threat); addressee and report role are unresolved from the supplied metadata that provides only stems and labels.

inquiry_patches.question: As a future conditional candidate only, if verified administration role and same-interview linkage hold: among asked-eligible interviews where the approach stem was answered in the affirmative, how do responses to the felt-threat and physical-threat stems diverge?
inquiry_patches.alternatives: Approach without threat vs approach with felt-only threat vs approach with physical threat; payoff would be separating access pressure from felt and physical-threat reports, subject to verified administration role, same-interview linkage, asked/eligible route and denominator, and with no cross-sectional or causal claims.
inquiry_patches.ceiling: Only after verified administration role, same-interview linkage, asked/eligible route and denominator are established; no claim about respondent risk, observed relation, physical exposure, or event cause; physical threat wording is not treated as actual endangerment.
